text: The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the Simeonites, clan by clan. Their inheritance lay within the inheritance of Judah.
Their inheritance included Beersheba, also called Sheba, then Moladah,

versions.text: Their inheritance included Beersheba (or Sheba), Moladah,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew lists Beersheba and Sheba as two names; the parenthetical "(or Sheba)" reads awkwardly aloud and leaves the reader unsure whether one town or two is meant. A footnote could note that the Hebrew reads "Beersheba and Sheba," while the total of thirteen towns suggests the two names refer to one place.

text: Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem,
Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susah,
Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen—thirteen towns with their villages;
Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan—four towns with their villages;
together with all the villages surrounding these towns as far as Baalath Beer, that is, Ramah of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the Simeonites, clan by clan.
The inheritance of the Simeonites was taken from the territory of Judah, because Judah's share was more than they needed. So the Simeonites received their inheritance within Judah's territory.
The third lot came up for Zebulun, clan by clan. The border of their inheritance ran as far as Sarid.
From there it went west to Maralah, touched Dabbesheth, and reached the ravine near Jokneam.
From Sarid it turned east toward the sunrise, to the border of Kisloth Tabor, then went on to Daberath and up to Japhia.
From there it continued eastward to Gath Hepher and Eth Kazin, came out at Rimmon, and turned toward Neah.
From there the border curved north of Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Iphtah El.

versions.text: There the border swung around on the north to Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Iphtah El.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מִצְּפוֹן חַנָּתֹן means "on the north of Hannathon," not "on the north to Hannathon." The revised wording is both more accurate and smoother for reading aloud.

text: Included were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem—twelve towns with their villages.
These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the Zebulunites, clan by clan.
The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for the Issacharites, clan by clan.
Their territory included Jezreel, Kesulloth, Shunem,
Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,
Remeth, En Gannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez.
The border touched Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth Shemesh, and ended at the Jordan—sixteen towns with their villages.
These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Issachar, clan by clan.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of Asher, clan by clan.
Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Acshaph,
Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal. On the west the border touched Carmel and Shihor Libnath.
It then turned east toward Beth Dagon, touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah El, and went north to Beth Emek and Neiel, passing Cabul on the left.
It went on to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.

versions.text: It went on to Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew text reads Ebron (עֶבְרֹן); Abdon reflects a variant in some manuscripts. Follow the Hebrew in the text and note the variant in a footnote: "Some manuscripts read Abdon."

text: The border then turned back toward Ramah and went to the fortified city of Tyre, turned toward Hosah, and came out at the sea in the region of Aczib,
along with Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob—twenty-two towns with their villages.
These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Asher, clan by clan.
The sixth lot came out for Naphtali, for the Naphtalites, clan by clan.
Their border ran from Heleph and the great tree in Zaanannim, past Adami Nekeb and Jabneel to Lakkum, and ended at the Jordan.
The border then turned west through Aznoth Tabor and came out at Hukkok. It touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.

versions.text: The border then turned west through Aznoth Tabor and came out at Hukkok. It touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.
versions.explanation: No change to the wording is needed, but a footnote would help the reader here: the mention of Judah in the far north is textually difficult, and some understand it as a reference to a place or clan bearing that name.

versions.text: It touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.
versions.explanation: The first half of the Hebrew verse is missing: וְשָׁב הַגְּבוּל יָמָּה אַזְנוֹת תָּבוֹר וְיָצָא מִשָּׁם חוּקֹקָה ("the border turned west to Aznoth Tabor and went out from there to Hukkok"). The stated reason for the previous revision was only to add a footnote about Judah, not to remove wording, so this content was dropped accidentally. Restoring the earlier wording also repairs the pronoun "It," which currently has no antecedent within the verse.

text: The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Kinnereth,
Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,
Kedesh, Edrei, En Hazor,
Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh—nineteen towns with their villages.
These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Naphtali, clan by clan.
The seventh lot came out for the tribe of Dan, clan by clan.
The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir Shemesh,
Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,
Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon,
Me Jarkon, and Rakkon, with the border facing Joppa.

But the territory of the Danites proved too small for them, so they marched up and attacked Leshem. They captured it, put it to the sword, took possession of it, and settled there. They named Leshem Dan, after their ancestor Dan.
These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Dan, clan by clan.
When they had finished apportioning the land according to its boundaries, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.

versions.text: When they had finished dividing the land into its allotted portions, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
versions.explanation: לִגְבוּלֹתֶיהָ means "according to its boundaries," not "into its allotted portions"; the boundary language of the whole chapter is lost in the current rendering.

text: At the LORD's command they gave him the town he had asked for—Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He rebuilt the town and settled there.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families of the tribes of Israel assigned by lot at Shiloh, before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting. And so they finished dividing the land.
